what:
User preference (corrected twice in 2026-04-27 session, ahmedmmeky): when validating something that's verifiable via shell command (cat/ls/stat/grep), I should run the command myself via Bash tool instead of asking the user to do it.

Pattern of corrections this session:
1. First correction: I asked user to run `cat /private/tmp/aide-cursor-val/.aide/cache/recalled-paths-<sid>.txt` to verify the tool_output→tool_response fix tracked IDs. They ran it (after I gave wrong path) and pasted contents. Should have run myself.
2. Second correction (explicit): "for commnd slike these you can easily verify, you can do it, can you do it for the last big hook output i sent to veirfy as needed?" — directly telling me to do verification myself.
3. Third corrective context: "you can check cat yourself" — same point, restated.

Apply to:
- Tracking-file inspection (.aide/cache/recalled-paths-<sid>.txt, correction-pending-<sid>.txt, etc.)
- Memory state verification (`node dist/cli/aide-memory.js list`)
- Rules-file content (grep/cat .cursor/rules/aide-memory.mdc)
- Build artifact mtimes (stat)
- Anything else where I have file access + know the path

Anti-pattern to avoid: writing pass/fail criteria for the user to verify when I could do the file-system verification myself. Those criteria are still useful for the parts that require the live agent + Cursor UI (hook OUTPUT blocks, agent behavior), but file-system state should be self-verified.

Bias correction in scope here too: don't shift verification work to the user when the Bash tool is available — even if the verification is "obvious" or seemingly trivial.
why: User explicitly corrected this twice in the same session. Without capturing as priority:always preference, the same pattern (asking user to run cat instead of doing it myself) will likely recur in future validation sessions across all projects. Marked priority:always so it auto-injects on session start; scoped project-wide because it's a behavioral preference, not file-specific.
